newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ship blocked by Japanese at disputed isle.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ship blocked by Japanese at disputed isle.

text.p: Japanese patrol boats have barred a private Taiwanese ship from nearing the disputed Diaoyu islands in the East China Sea, rekindling a sovereignty dispute, a Taipei newspaper said on Thursday.

The China Times Express carried front-page pictures of a Japanese coast guard vessel with a banner written in Chinese reading: "The Japanese government asks you to leave Japan's territorial waters at once."

The paper said it used a leased fishing boat on Wednesday to try to approach the uninhabited islands, where a Japanese right-wing group's construction of a makeshift lighthouse in July embroiled Taiwan, Japan and China in a sovereignty dispute.
The small Diaoyu chain lies about 300 km (190 miles) west of Okinawa and 200 km (125 miles) east of Taiwan and is claimed by Taipei, Tokyo and Beijing.
Apart from two patrol boats, Japan also sent a helicopter and used loudspeakers to urge the private boat to leave, the newspaper said.
"Our ship was escorted away," the newspaper said.
On Wednesday Tsang Kin-shing, a pro-democracy legislator in Hong Kong, said a group of about 20 people would sail to the Diaoyu Islands at the beginning of next month.
The latest incidents come at a time when the row over the Diaoyus appeared to have been calming down.
In July, members of the right-wing Japan Youth Federation sailed to the Diaoyu chain, known as the Senkakus in Japanese, and erected a five-metre (16-foot) aluminium lighthouse.
Patriotic passion ran high in Taiwan after the lighthouse was discovered and some 200 Taiwanese fishing boats threatened to storm the island to dismantle the structure.
The fishermen called off their protest in August after Tokyo sent fishery officials to Taiwan to discuss the simmering row despite a lack of diplomatic ties between the governments.
The Japanese group later backed down from plans to further assert Tokyo's claim to the islands.
Beijing and Tokyo remain deeply divided over their rival claims but China recently has toned down its angry rhetoric.

In 1990, Taiwanese threw eggs at Japan's unofficial embassy in Taipei after Japanese ships kept two Taiwanese boats from landing on the Diaoyus to plant a torch symbolising Taipei's claim to sovereignty.
Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government and Beijing's communist People's Republic that toppled it both assert that China has had sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
Tokyo's claim dates to Japan's military humiliation of China in 1895, when it wrested Taiwan and other Chinese territories as war booty to be used as a base for wider Asian conquests.
